content.title: About
content.content: Lemon cupcake is a soft, fragrant cake with a bright citrus flavor, made from flour, sugar, eggs, butter, and fresh lemon juice and zest. It is often served as a dessert with tea or coffee and can also be used as a base for a layered cake.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The lemon cupcake became popular in Europe in the 19th century as a light dessert for summer picnics.
The combination of lemon acidity and sweet batter creates a balanced taste that is enhanced by a powdered sugar glaze.
Traditionally the cupcake is baked in a “English” (English muffin) shape, but modern recipes use muffin or cupcake tins.
Lemon juice in the batter activates the leavening agents, making the cake more airy.
In some countries the lemon cupcake is decorated with lemon zest or finely chopped berries for a flavor contrast.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Lemons are rich in vitamin C, which supports the immune system and has antioxidant properties.

items.title: Low Fat Content
items.content: Compared with many sweet pastries, a lemon cupcake typically contains a moderate amount of butter, making it less fatty.

items.title: Dietary Fiber
items.content: Using whole‑grain flour in the recipe adds dietary fiber, which aids digestion.

items.title: Energy Boost
items.content: The mix of carbohydrates and a modest amount of protein provides a quick source of energy.

items.title: Mood Enhancement
items.content: Lemon aroma is known for its refreshing and calming effect, which can improve mood.

items.title: Citrus Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to lemons, such as skin rashes or swelling.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The high acidity of lemon juice can irritate the stomach in people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Sugar Content
items.content: Cupcakes often contain a notable amount of sugar, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Gluten Content
items.content: Traditional recipes use wheat flour, making the cupcake unsuitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Lemon cupcake can be served as a standalone dessert, sliced into bite‑size pieces and topped with powdered sugar glaze, buttercream, or fresh berries. It is also convenient to take on the go as a quick snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cupcake in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, keep it in the refrigerator – it will stay fresh for about a week. Bring the cupcake to room temperature before serving.
